questions.explain: Add matching cells: $(A+B)_{ij} = A_{ij} + B_{ij}$, e.g. $-2 + 1 = -1$ and $3 + (-1) = 2$. Multiplying matching cells is a different operation.

questions.q: Can you add a $2 \times 3$ matrix to a $3 \times 2$ matrix?
options: Only if both matrices are square
No — addition needs the same shape so every cell has a partner
Yes, after the result is reshaped
questions.explain: Matrix addition pairs cells with the same row and column, so the shapes must match exactly — having the same number of cells is not enough.

questions.q: With $k = 1.5$, a cell of $A$ equal to $-4$ becomes what in $kA$?
questions.explain: $(kA)_{ij} = k \times A_{ij} = 1.5 \times (-4) = -6$. Adding $k$ instead of multiplying gives $-2.5$.

questions.q: What does the scalar $k = -1$ do to a matrix?
options: Flips the sign of every cell, keeping their sizes
questions.explain: Every cell is multiplied by the same $-1$, so all signs flip and the sizes stay the same. Swapping rows and columns is the transpose.
